title: Vines Swallowed Five Hundred Houses On This Chinese Island

basis.note: median of recent videos blended with the niche benchmark; learning gated until day 5

predicted_range.basis: about 3x either way, from backtested error (274 of our own videos so far)

segments.narration: Vines have swallowed five hundred houses on one island. Houtouwan clings to a slope on Shengshan Island, sixty-four kilometres east of Shanghai.
It went up in the 1950s for fishing, and it worked. More than two thousand fishermen and their families lived on that hillside.
So what empties a village that size? No storm, no disaster. A ferry timetable and a school run.
Shengshan's boats could not compete with Shanghai's fleets, and the island had no reliable transport, schooling or work. By 1994 a handful were left.
By 2002 it was empty. The green took the walls so completely that tourists now pay to walk through a village made of leaves.
